model.description: One row per location, calendar year, age grouping and age group, for the world total and every country or area the provider publishes. The table carries the same population twice over: once in the provider's twenty-one five-year age groups, and once in the three broad groups summed from them.
model.name: world_demography_age_structure

questions.derivation: Select the five-year grouping's bands for the location and year, ordered by the first year of age, with the male and female populations in each.
questions.question: What is a location's population by age and sex in a given year?

questions.derivation: Select the broad grouping's three bands for the location and year, with each band's share of that year's population.
questions.question: What share of a location's population is young, of working age, or old?

questions.derivation: Select a band's share of the population by year, within either grouping, with the estimate or projection marker for that year.

temporal.meaning: Each period is the first day of the calendar year the observation describes, from the provider's Time column. Populations are measured on 1 July of that year. The grain is one row per period, location_id, age_grouping and age_group, and the two groupings describe the same people: a consumer that mixes them counts everyone twice. Within a grouping the bands are exhaustive and do not overlap, so their totals sum to the location's population and their shares sum to one hundred. The panel is rectangular: every location carries every year from 1950 to 2100 and every band in both groupings. Years up to the snapshot's represented date are the provider's estimates and later years are its medium-scenario projection, which series_kind records. The top band of the five-year grouping and the old band of the broad grouping are open-ended, which age_end records as null.

validations.description: There is exactly one observation for each location, calendar year, age grouping and age band.
validations.name: one-row-per-location-year-grouping-and-band

validations.description: Period, location identity, grouping markers, band identity and the three populations are never null.
validations.name: required-identity-and-population

validations.description: Every country or area carries an ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 code, and only the world total does not.
validations.name: only-the-world-total-lacks-an-iso3-code

validations.description: For each location and year, the five-year bands and the broad bands sum to the same total, so neither grouping is missing or double-counting anyone.
validations.name: the-two-groupings-describe-the-same-population

validations.description: Male and female populations sum to the band total, to the precision the provider publishes.
validations.name: the-sexes-sum-to-the-band-total

validations.description: Each grouping's bands account for the whole population of the location and year, so their shares sum to one hundred.
validations.name: shares-sum-to-one-hundred-within-a-grouping

validations.description: Within a grouping the bands cover every age from zero upward without a gap or an overlap, and exactly one band is open-ended at the top.
validations.name: bands-are-exhaustive-and-do-not-overlap

validations.description: Every location carries the same years and every location-year the same bands, so a consumer reaching any year finds a complete structure.
validations.name: the-panel-is-rectangular

validations.description: No band carries a negative population.
validations.name: populations-are-never-negative
